content: Seed is a private local-first companion system.
Seed is a private local-first companion. Not a random chatbot.
Built Seed v0.1 local terminal core with menu control, Seed_Core.md reading, memory_rules.md reading, first_contact.md reading, JSON memory, and journal files.
Added safe JSON memory functions: load memories, save memories, add memory, list memories, search memories by type, and delete memories by number.

Refactored Seed into modules: seed_cli.py for menu control, seed_memory.py for memory, seed_journal.py for journal, seed_files.py for Markdown files, seed_status.py for status, and seed_brain.py for Ollama connection.
Added memory quality upgrades: allowed memory type validation, created_at timestamps, old memory compatibility with memory.get(), and cleaner memory printing.
Added Seed system status screen showing version, required file status, memory count, allowed memory type count, LLM status, and local terminal mode.
Connected Seed to local Ollama using llama3.1:8b through the Ollama HTTP API and requests.post().
Added Talk to Seed in seed_cli.py. Seed now sends user messages
Seed gave an incomplete progress summary because the actual project progress was not saved into seed_memory.json yet.
A memory-aware Seed can only use memories that are actually stored. Unsaved progress is invisible to Seed.
seed_brain.py is currently active. The Talk to Seed option in seed_cli.py calls ask_seed() from seed_brain.py, which builds the prompt and sends it to Ollama.
Updated Seed_Core.md and status/menu version to Seed v0.2.3 so Seed's identity file matches its current actual capabilities.
Seed v0.2.3 now gives structured progress summaries using stored memories. It groups project progress into phases and answers based on memory context instead of guessing.
Seed's answers improve when important progress is saved as structured memories. Memory quality directly affects answer quality.
Added Seed v0.2.4 session chat mode. Talk to Seed now supports multiple messages in one chat and uses temporary session_history for follow-up questions.
Seed now has two memory layers: short-term session history for the current chat and long-term JSON memory for intentional saved memories.
Seed initially asked to save temporary test phrases too often. The prompt rules needed to more clearly separate temporary chat context from important long-term memory.
Added /save command inside Talk to Seed so memories can be saved without leaving chat.
Added /save command inside Talk to Seed so memories can be saved without leaving chat
Seed v0.2.5 added intentional memory saving from chat. The /save command saves long-term memories without leaving Talk to Seed and also updates session_history so Seed knows what was just saved.
SSeed now separates temporary session context from intentional long-term memory. /save acts as the bridge between short-term chat and permanent JSON memory.
Seed v0.2.9 added /debug context inspection. Seed can now show relevant memories, recent journal entries, and current session history for debugging context
Seed's behavior depends heavily on prompt context. The /debug command helps inspect what the model actually sees before answering.

Fixed /journal session context. write_journal() now returns the saved journal entry, and talk_to_seed() adds the exact journal entry text into session_history so Seed can answer what was written during the same chat.
Added recent journal injection. seed_journal_py can return recent journal entries, and seed_brain.py injects them into the prompt so Seed can use recent free-form journal context
Connected Seed to local Ollama llama3.1:8b using requests.post() and the Ollama HTTP API at localhost:11434/api/generate
Seed v0.3.3 added minimum relevance filtering. Memory retrieval now requires keyword matches before importance ranking, so unrelated high-importance memories do not appear in search results.
Importance and relevance are different. Seed should prefer memories that match the current question, then use importanc eto rank them.
Seed v0.3.4 added memory search score visibility. /search now shows keyword_score and total_score so retrieval decisions are easier to debug.
Seeing retrieval scores make Seed's memory system more transparent. Debuggable retrieval is necessary before adding more advanced memory features.
User progress update: we added automatic memory suggestions and it works
Seed V0.6.0 added a usability and control command pack inside Talk to Seed, including /suggest, /autosuggest, /forget, /journal-read, /core, and /clear-session.
Seed's chat mode is becoming a controlled local shell where slash commands manage memory, journal, status, debug, and session behavior while normal text goes to the model.
Fixed self-edit syntax test behavior, confirmed working.
Seed's memory system became more companion-like because Altan no longer has to manually classify every memory; Seed can draft the classification while Altan keeps final approval.

Seed v1.13.0 added the Companion Cockpit and Seed World Kernel. It introduced seed_world.py and seed_cockpit.py, persistent Seed World state, Memory Garden counters, life timeline events, quests, rituals, local FastAPI cockpit, browser dashboard, local API endpoints, browser chat, World context injection, and HUD World visibility.
User progress update: tell me what changed
